reply: Based on the provided document, treason consists in levying war against the United States or adhering to its enemies and giving them aid and comfort [1]. No person can be convicted of treason unless there is testimony from two witnesses to the same overt act [1] or a confession in open court [1]; conviction requires both. Additionally, Congress has the power to declare punishments for treason, but no one can be "attainted" (deprived of rights) except during their own lifetime [1]. Furthermore, citizens fleeing into another state and refusing to surrender on demand may be required by that other state to be delivered up to its jurisdiction over the crime [2], though they cannot avoid labor or service in the new location due to laws there unless claimed against them.
